title: The Russian MoD Said It Intercepted 269 Ukrainian Drones Overnight. The Same Window Saw a Third Strike on Poltavskaya's 28-Tank Fuel Depot, the Tavrida and Balaklava Thermal Plants Hit in Crimea, and Four Cities Blacked Out. Kondratyev Did Not Post on Telegram About the Krasnodar Fire
narrative:
On the night of 24-25 June 2026, the Russian Ministry of Defence announced that air-defence forces had intercepted and destroyed 269 Ukrainian drones between 20:00 MSK on 24 June and 07:00 MSK on 25 June. The Russian briefing listed 12 Russian regions, occupied Crimea, and the Black Sea as affected: Belgorod, Bryansk, Volgograd, Kaluga, Kursk, Oryol, Saratov, Smolensk, Rostov, Tula, Krasnodar Krai, Moscow region, plus Crimea and the Black Sea. Separately, the Ukrainian Air Force reported a Russian strike consisting of one Iskander-M ballistic missile and 90 attack drones — Shahed, Gerbera, Italmas, and Parody decoy types — of which it said air defence destroyed or suppressed 83. The two narratives — 'we neutralised their 269' vs 'we neutralised 83 of their 90' — were presented on the same calendar day, for the same air domain, in mutually exclusive framings of total throughput.

The Krasnoarmeysky district head Alexander Kharitonov, in a Max-platform post, framed the Poltavskaya fuel-depot fire as a consequence of 'falling UAV debris' — a downed-drone aftermath rather than a direct hit. The Russian-installed governor of Krasnodar Krai, Veniamin Kondratyev, did not write on his official Telegram channel about the event at all. On the Crimean side, the Russian-installed governor Mikhail Razvozhayev blamed the Sevastopol power outage on 'an overload of the electricity network outside the region' rather than on the overnight drone strikes, and the occupation authorities declared an air-threat alert only after 02:00 — hours after drones had been airborne, according to Krymskyi Veter.

analysis:
The Russian MoD's 269-intercept framing and the Ukrainian Air Force's 83-of-90 framing are presented on the same calendar day, for the same air domain, as mutually exclusive framings of total throughput. Both are claims of operational success; both cannot be simultaneously true at the throughput each asserts. The 269 figure for overnight 24-25 June is structurally parallel to the 323 figure MoD announced for overnight 23-24 June (covered in the prior 24-25 June piece) — both are aggregate counts that the same MoD statement's regional breakdown cannot actually support. The 12-region list plus Crimea and the Black Sea is itself an admission that intercept coverage is geographically thin: a 'successful intercept' campaign that touches a fifth of Russia's federal subjects is operationally incoherent as a denial claim.

The third Poltavskaya strike in three weeks is the load-bearing physical-evidence layer. The Poltavskaya Neftebaza OJSC facility — 28 tanks, 14,950 m³ capacity, supplying fuel to Krasnodar Krai and the Republic of Adygea — was struck on 5-6 June, 15-16 June, and now 24-25 June 2026. The 5-6 June strike produced a 5,000 m² fire and a FIRMS thermal anomaly at coordinates 45.221684, 39.684261 logged at 04:11 local time. The 24-25 June strike set three storage tanks ablaze, one of them full, per Exilenova+. An air-defence kill-chain that returns a third fire at a single fuel depot over three weeks is not delivering the protective outcome the MoD's success count claims. The structural finding is that an aggregate 'destroyed 269' count over a 12-region distribution implies thinner coverage per site than the 83/90 figure (1 ballistic + 6 strike UAVs reaching 7 locations, 16 debris-fall locations).

The Russian-official downplay pattern is symmetric across two governors and one district head. Kharitonov's 'falling UAV debris' framing treats a third fire at a known fuel-storage site as aftermath rather than direct hit. Razvozhayev's 'network overload' framing is contradicted by the temporally-correlated Tavrida + Balaklava thermal-plant strike sequence and the partisan ATESH claim that the attack 'covered the entire occupied peninsula.' Most structurally telling is Kondratyev's silence: the Russian-installed governor of Krasnodar Krai, where two of the three Poltavskaya strikes have occurred, did not post on his official Telegram channel about the 24-25 June fire at all. The silence is the mirror image of the public statements — neither framing the event as debris nor denying it, simply refusing to acknowledge it.

The Crimean layer adds a thermal-plant strike that the prior 24-25 June 323-drone article did not cover. Tavrida thermal power plant (near Simferopol) and Balaklava thermal power plant (Sevastopol) were both struck overnight. Power failed in Simferopol, Yalta (full blackout), parts of Yevpatoria, Pervomaiske, Krasnoperekopsk, and Bakhchysarai. Sevastopol lost power without schedule, and a powerful explosion was logged near the Kacha military airfield at approximately 04:00. The Crimean Railway reduced trains to/from Crimea from 18 per day to 7 per day per Aksyonov. Razvozhayev's 'network overload outside the region' formulation is the verbatim denial language that the Tavrida strike sequence and the ATESH 'entire occupied peninsula' formulation directly contradict.

The 20 Russian regions with gasoline-sales restrictions (Meduza, Moscow Times) are the downstream demand-side effect the MoD's framing structurally elides. Gas stations in occupied Crimea were instructed to fully suspend fuel sales to civilians from 21 June per Kyiv Independent. An air-defence success count that returns regional fuel-sales restrictions and a Crimean fuel-sales suspension is a count that has been disconnected from the protective outcome it claims.

Zelenskyy's 24 June nightly address provides the structural explanation that may account for the throughput asymmetry without resolving the contradiction. Russia is moving 'nearly 90 launchers deployed to Valdai from [other] regions of Russia' — i.e. a concentration of Russian AD assets onto a handful of priority sites, leaving peripheral regions with thinner coverage. The 269-intercept count over a 12-region distribution is consistent with this reallocation pattern: more intercepts spread thinner. But the same reallocation pattern is also consistent with the third Poltavskaya fire and the Tavrida + Balaklava thermal-plant strikes — the sites the reallocation left under-defended are exactly the sites that burned.
verdict: [SIPHONED VERDICT]: On the night of 24-25 June 2026, the Russian MoD's 269-intercept framing and the Ukrainian Air Force's 83-of-90 framing were both presented as operational successes for the same air domain on the same day. The third Poltavskaya strike in three weeks — 28 tanks, 14,950 m³ capacity, FIRMS thermal history — is the load-bearing physical-evidence layer that an aggregate 'destroyed 269' count cannot accommodate. The Tavrida + Balaklava thermal-plant strikes, four-city blackout, and Kacha airfield explosion at ~04:00 are the Crimean layer that Razvozhayev's 'network overload' framing directly contradicts. Kondratyev's documented Telegram silence on the third Krasnodar fire in three weeks is the downplay-by-omission mirror image of Kharitonov's 'falling UAV debris' framing. The 20-region gasoline-sales restrictions and the Crimean fuel-sales suspension are the demand-side effects the intercept count elides. Beat-distinct from the 323-drone article of 24-25 June (different number, different facilities, this article covers the Poltavskaya third-strike history, Tavrida/Balaklava thermal-plant layer, Kacha airfield, Crimean Railway 18→7 cut, and Kondratyev Telegram silence — none of which the 323 article addressed).
